module_mood_contract: calibrated trust, not-knowing flavour: a kept check that says what it cannot see; trust centre of Day 2

stealing_the_mood: close L104-L106 asserts a catch ("It found something") as fact, so a clean-result student reads a recap of someone else's run

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the agentic design — no human backstops.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L56 "Don't read the four files as they land. The scorer reads them." and L31 "Don't open the briefing."; no human backstop on agent flows, judgement sits with the scorer agent (hallucination-bakeoff-5 "name ONE winner") and the human decision is the keep at L90. Harm (exhaustive if-then rulesets, manual observation) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: One exercise = one bounded activity.
rules_evaluated.evidence: one bounded activity: plant, check four ways, score, keep the winner, run it on a real summary (L7). Closest sub-division is the five "Phase" headers (L21-L92); they are the do-observe-adjust arc of ONE benchmark, not sub-numbered exercises.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Modules composable across variants.
rules_evaluated.evidence: shared library by key: L17/L27/L35/L47/L52/L66/L72/L76/L86 reuse Agents 101 hallucination-bakeoff-1..8 by marker, with the runtime fork at L45-L53 as a div pair; no -variant fork file; audience framing is the trio roles (L11-L15) and the two new apt101-d2 prompts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Three-level completeness.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L113-L129: Role in Day 2, Reuse, Artefacts, Leap test chain strategy frame (trust centre) to runtime artifacts (module-5/*, judges/groundedness-judge.md) to the sendable asset team/<name>/judge-run.md (L121); a stranger can read back from judge-run to the strategy line. Harm (a chain that stops at an unconsumed artefact) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pattern-recognition LOs need n≥2 instances with contrast.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the LO is spotting made-up claims; n>=2 with contrast: 30 pooled claims against four methods (hallucination-bakeoff-2/-3) and then a second exposure on a real summary nobody planted anything in (L96-L102). Closest to violating is L92-L102 being one real read; the planted corpus supplies the contrast.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Progression-with-variations is the spine.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the move is the benchmark-then-keep move reused from Agents 101 M5 (L115 "unchanged"), with a new face per this training: the post-it prediction (L64), the pre-registered bet (L15) and the real-summary run (L98). Same model, different instance. Earning-point obligations: none moved. Harm (verbatim repetition inviting the skim) absent because phase 5 is a new instance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student agency — adults decide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest forced pacing L56 "Don't read the four files as they land." and L31 "Don't open the briefing."; L31 guards the blind main session that the benchmark depends on, so skipping creates a dead end (a contaminated benchmark), the rule's own exception; L56 spares a reading burden rather than pacing. Adults still decide the summary they check (L15).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Delegation — student brings, Claude screens.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L15 "a research summary from your team's drive": access is handled in the fence, "Where a source isn't on this laptop, write its name and \"not here\"" (apt101-d2-ready-a-real-summary); picking the summary and the bet is the student's (L15), screening is the judge's. Harm (a step Claude cannot reach, or a pick made for the student) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Split mega-exercise when phases = distinct skills + distinct artifacts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: N phases but one skill (checking claims) and a mechanical chain: briefing to claim pool to detectors to scorer to judge to real run, with no cognitive break (L25-L98). Counter-condition holds, so it stays one exercise; phase 5 reuses the phase 4 artifact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-realism check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: every named path has a producer: ./crux.md, module-3/stances/, memory/, sources/ are in Consumes (L120) and produced by gather the evidence and grow the tree; module-5/* are produced inside this exercise (L121); judges/groundedness-judge.md by hallucination-bakeoff-8; team/<name>/ by the ready prompt. Nothing needs an uninstalled tool. Harm (a blocker mid-run) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Teach principle + technique — default.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L41 "Each check is a different method on the same claim pool, run in its own subagent" and L62 (precision and recall in plain words) give WHY, and hallucination-bakeoff-6 teaches the columns from the student's own rows; HOW is in the prompts the student runs. No black-box invocation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: forcing functions sit in fences: "force the pick" and "strict substring match" (hallucination-bakeoff-5), "Stay narrow" and "under 20 lines" (hallucination-bakeoff-8), "quote the sentence ... or write \"not found\"" (apt101-d2-judge-a-real-summary), "Don't check it." (ready prompt). Closest body-only move is L64 post-it prediction: a room move with no Claude to receive it, so a fence is impossible (boundary 2 reasoning). Count-scripts: L74 "one sentence each" mirrors the fence's own "one-sentence answer"; treated under 27, not here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Personal-first, team promotion via human conversation.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L90 "the team lead copies judges/groundedness-judge.md and module-5/ to team/<team lead's name>/. The other two ask Claude to copy both into their own training folder": the judge lands personally first, then a person carries it to the team folder; nothing auto-promotes and no shared infra is changed by the agent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verification layers sample DIFFERENT error distributions — not belt-and-braces.
rules_evaluated.evidence: four methods that sample different error shapes (source triangulation, entailment, citation integrity, counter-evidence: hallucination-bakeoff-3) plus a fifth scorer agent plus the human bet on a real summary (L15, L102). No layer is dropped on "others will catch". Harm (single-layer done) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cohort execution is trainer-paced + concurrent, not sequential.
rules_evaluated.evidence: timing budgets are concurrent: L3 "Phase 1 ~10, Phase 2 ~7, Phase 3 ~18, Phase 4 ~10, Phase 5 ~10, close ~5" and the maintainer Timing (L127) explain why phase 5 is 10 (readied during phases 1-2); designed so two seats prepare while one drives (L123). Not a sum of demo and execute.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Host-skill optional; maintainer blocks trainer-only.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c -i -E "nerd|teacher claude|host-skill" -> 0 on the file; the maintainer block names the trainer-facing moves as Watch-fors (L125), with no host-skill as actor.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats: in-chat over file-write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: every file write has a downstream reader: evidence-roster/briefing read by the claim and detector prompts, detectors read by the scorer (hallucination-bakeoff-5), scoreboard by the judge-writer, real-summary.md by apt101-d2-judge-a-real-summary, judge-run.md by keep and run tonight (L121). Closest (c)-only candidate is adjudicated-claims.md, but the scorer reads it before scoring (bakeoff-5). Reflection itself (L74 surprise lines) stays in chat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L64 "the team lead reads the four methods aloud ... Each of you writes on a post-it ... Face down until the scoreboard lands." and L68 "Turn the post-its over. Whoever called it says what they saw that the others didn't; whoever missed says what they trusted instead." are authored room conversation with a prescribed utterance, as are L74 "Each of you answers its question about what surprised you, one sentence each, and the team lead types all three." and L102 "Then tell your two teammates which line it was". Harm the rule prevents: curriculum body scripting cohort management (compare, share, confess) that the trainer reads off the room; harm present at L68 (a compare-and-confess round in student text) and in the count of room cues (L64, L66, L68, L74, L78, L102) against the third carve-out's one-line ceiling. Mitigators: the trio is the delivery unit (Room, L123) and the post-it prediction (L64) is the work of a prediction contest; no dated accept-note covers it (accept_notes holds only the Quality stamp, L110); no pause cue or "compare with" string (grep -c -i -E "compare with|next to you|neighbo|tell the room|discuss" -> 0). Sibling precedent: build-your-product-memory REVISE on a prescribed read-out; gather-the-evidence and five-users PASS where the read-out serves a group-owned artefact.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Keep the post-it prediction as the work move; cut the second sentence of L68 (who says what) and reduce L102 to the flagged line, leaving compare and share to the trainer; or have the maintainer add a dated accept-note naming the trio as the delivery unit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Eval = fixed yardstick; thing measured learns.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L62-L70: the scorer is one fixed fifth agent that adjudicates once and scores all four methods against that single reference (hallucination-bakeoff-5); the judge kept at L84 is not rewritten inside the loop. The measured thing (detector methods) is what varies. Harm (a rewritable yardstick) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reading burden for verification = banned. Claude audits Claude.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L88 "Open judges/groundedness-judge.md. Under twenty lines, named for what it does, with a Known limit: line" asks the student to read the saved judge for shape and specificity, not to check Claude output for correctness against sources; correctness checking is done by the scorer (L62) and the judge (L98). L56 "Don't read the four files as they land" removes the burden. This exercise is the verification module that teaches Claude auditing Claude.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-report + self-audit charity — verify at artifact, over-flag or fresh-session for critique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: summary is never the end of a phase: L25 and hallucination-bakeoff-1 ("do not summarize the briefing in chat") send the student to files; L88 "Open judges/groundedness-judge.md"; self-audit is cold: the scorer is a fifth agent (L62) and the briefing was written in a separate worker (L25), and bakeoff-5 matches by strict substring rather than by the scorer's own charity. Closest: L106 recap states results; it follows the artifacts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Offered structures need forced-engagement mechanic.
rules_evaluated.evidence: offered structure is the judge file and the Known limit line; forced engagement is explicit: L88 "Push back if the limit says something like \"quality is hard\". It should describe one kind of claim this judge will let through." and L78 push-back on a surprise "that could belong to anyone". Harm (90% take verbatim) countered in both places.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source-type blindness on ingestion.
rules_evaluated.evidence: dosage test: the default ingest path is markdown memory and retrieval files (Consumes, L120: memory/, sources/), not slide-format exports; the real-summary route (L15) may meet a deck or PDF, a minority branch on which the "not here" fallback and the judge's "not found" report the gap loudly. An addition is not owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Task selection drives outcome → name floor AND ceiling.
rules_evaluated.evidence: floor and ceiling are named: hallucination-bakeoff-1 "at least 5 and at most 20 files total" for the roster, and L15 bounds the real run to one summary. Harm (epic-sized selection) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer-block hedge naming section's own failure mode = cut-signal, not warning.
rules_evaluated.evidence: not a cut-signal: the Watch-for hedges (L125) name failures recoverable by a clearer body line, not a premise that can be misread; premise-test: remove the L125 hedges and the section is still defensible. Note the clean-result Watch-for is addressed under strategy tie-in rule 1 (close 7/10) because L102 and L106 presume a flag.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audience tier determines authoring substrate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Builder-leader tier (product trio): the kept judge is a plain markdown file (hallucination-bakeoff-8 "Write the judge as a markdown file to judges/groundedness-judge.md"), no plugin install; the audience can use it on Day 1 of the exercise without an install step stealing the teaching moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verification machinery needs smoke-test before trust.
rules_evaluated.evidence: verification machinery is measured before it is trusted: the winning method was run on 30 planted claims and scored (L62, hallucination-bakeoff-5) before being rewritten as a judge (L84); L90 "When the judge is right" gates the copy; phase 5 prompt reports each flag with the supporting sentence or "not found". Closest gap: the portable rewrite itself is first invoked on real data at L98, mitigated by the evidence quote it must return.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Symmetric visible-mechanics > runtime fork when dual-runtime constraints break agentic move.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the one fork (L45-L53, bakeoff-3 vs -4) changes only subagent to agent; both runtimes stay agentic, which is the case where a fork is right. No manual-versus-agent asymmetry.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Load-bearing platform feature = no fallback. Gate or redesign.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c -i -E "if your environment|instead and treat" -> 0; the central move (four parallel detectors) has no fallback offered; the Cowork fork keeps the same parallel agents (L51-L53).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Plug points + UX.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (a) grep -c "## Plug Points" -> 0, no plug-point section in an exercise; (b) walking prompt to prompt: paths are discoverable (module-5/, judges/, team/<my-name>/), hand-off from L90 names created artifacts, no megaprompt beyond bakeoff-3 and -5 which are single copies. Closest "wait, what" is `<my-name>` in the two apt101-d2 fences, resolved by corpus convention (14 registry prompts use it).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test — 3 observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L129 "Leap test": (1) runs judges/groundedness-judge.md on the next research summary before it reaches a priority call, (2) says which method won and what its known limit misses, (3) has one real claim the judge flagged that someone would otherwise have repeated. Each is an artifact-or-act a PM can tell Monday; (3) is the loosest but names a countable claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch.
rules_evaluated.evidence: maintainer Watch-fors (L125) pair a failure mode with a recovery for the phases that carry forcing functions: reading the briefing before extraction (recover: re-plant), a detector's paraphrased flags (read its file), scorer hedging (re-run, force a pick, ensemble cap two), judge sprawl, generic Known limit, clean real summary. Gap closest: the opening phase's pre-registered bet (L15) has no named failure mode (vague or already-checked bet); non-blocking suggestion filed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L43 "All four run at once. If one starts reading far beyond the evidence, stop it, steer it narrower, then say \"continue\"." covers the over-reading direction only. Fan-out signal: four parallel subagents (hallucination-bakeoff-3) each reading the roster files. grep -c -i -E "so far|premature|more here|too early" on the file -> 0. Harm the rule prevents: a detector that skims and declares done scores low recall and is read as a weak method, so the winner is decided by a quiet quit; the harm is present (a streaming run masks the shallow finish).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add the premature-stop direction beside the over-reading steer: a detector that finishes fast with almost nothing flagged is told there is more here and continues.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Save belongs with authoring, not loading.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the create exercise ends with the artifact in its production location: L90 copies judges/groundedness-judge.md and module-5/ to team/<name>/ and into each folder at the same paths; the use exercises (choose the bet, keep and run tonight) open from the saved file. Both runtimes share the same steps.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Convenience-driven prompts with known shape-bias → body acknowledgment callout.
rules_evaluated.evidence: bakeoff-5 grades several detectors in one turn, an accepted convenience, mitigated in-fence by "strict substring match", "Do not return all four are useful" and the cap-two ensemble; bakeoff-1 knowingly invites softening ("You cannot make that number precise") and counters with "Do not hedge". Both are load-bearing for the benchmark, not accidental, so no callout is owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Deliberate-antipattern prompts = class-judge exempt, flagged-by-design.
rules_evaluated.evidence: hallucination-bakeoff-1 is a deliberate antipattern ("blend in general knowledge. Do not hedge.") because the planted fabrication IS the test corpus; behavior judges flagging niceness-tax there are accepted-by-design. Flagged risk equals what the prompt demonstrates.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose must not supply an answer its prompt asks for — position is not the test (widened 2026-08-12).
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L62 "of what it flagged, how much was really made up, and of what was made up, how much it caught" defines the two columns before hallucination-bakeoff-6 asks Claude to explain them; it teaches how to READ the scoreboard coming (legal shape) and the prompt's own value (which matters more for catching fabrication, from the student's rows) is not supplied. L5-L7 "What you do" names artifacts and activity only (axes a, b, c). L78 names a BAD answer shape ("the scoreboard was interesting"), legal. Note L106 recap asserts the real-run result as fact (see strategy 1).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Callouts next to prompts: steer, don't pre-empt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the only failure-mode callout beside a fence is L43, and it is the steering shape (notice, stop it, steer it narrower, continue), not a pre-empted named ghost; L88 push-back is likewise generic. Harm (a callout rotting behind a changed prompt) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer blocks point, don't restate. Link architecture doc where they touch delivery.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the maintainer block carries what is unique (Role, Reuse, Artefacts, Room, Watch-fors, Timing, Leap test); delivery mechanics are not restated (no working-dir or install paragraphs). Closest L115 "Paths stay module-5/ as the prompts write them" is a one-line pointer. Nothing to rot.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module prerequisite rescue: run it late, never fabricate.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: receiving inputs are same-day exercise outputs (crux.md, stances, memory), not a prior module's send-off run that may be absent

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Story and depth are judged per big learning that develops, never per feature that recurs.
rules_evaluated.evidence: cold read, the big learning planted-complicated-paid: "a check you can run is only as good as what it can see" is planted by the planted claims (L7), complicated by the post-it prediction against the scoreboard (L64-L68) and the winner's Known limit (L88), and paid on a summary nobody planted anything in (L96-L102), named only after the student did it (L106). Depth is one learning developing, not a recurring figure.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: registry fences carry no bracket placeholders; closest `<my-name>` in apt101-d2-ready-a-real-summary and apt101-d2-judge-a-real-summary is a path segment resolved by the corpus convention (14 registry prompts use it; Day 1 sets the team folder), not an invented slot. The ready prompt's trailing "The summary:" is a legitimate open-hook (student has the value, Claude cannot propose it).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L15 lead-in "Then ask Claude to get it ready, and say which claim you would bet is unsupported before any judge exists." sits above a fence that ends in a dangling colon ("The summary:"). Rule 2 sub-case: the lead-in's whole job is naming what to drop in, and it never says to drop the summary after the colon. Harm: a student is left to infer the fill-in slot (the persona unsure what goes after the colon); present, mild. Other lead-ins (L25 31 words over a long multi-step fence, L84 17 words, L98) stay inside.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Replace the lead-in sentence with the slot: drop the summary after the colon, then the claim you would bet is unsupported.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the file uses markers on their own lines (L17, L27, L35, L47, L52, L66, L72, L76, L86, L100); the expander reconstructs **Prompt** *(Claude Code)* then the fence (expand-md output reviewed); no copy-prefix or closer. grep -c "^\*\*Prompt\*\*" on the source -> 0 inline blocks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chains name deterministic paths: bakeoff-2 opens module-5/briefing.md, bakeoff-3 reads claim-pool, briefing and roster by path, judge-a-real-summary reads team/<my-name>/real-summary.md "if I readied one" with an ask-me fallback for first-create intent. Harm (filename drift creating a second file) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest hallucination-bakeoff-1 "so the detectors have something to catch": the planter is told detectors follow, which is load-bearing (it sets the plant rate), and it does not pre-check, defer, or invoke detectors. The detector prompts do not name the scorer beyond the strict substring rule that the scorer needs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c -i -E "/clear|new session|fresh session|new conversation" over the ten registry bodies -> 0 (planted "open a new session now" returns 1, so the pattern works); isolation is by subagent (bakeoff-1, -3).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c -E "\*\*|\*[A-Za-z]" over the ten prompt bodies (frontmatter stripped) -> 0 (planted "a **bold** and *it*" returns 1); emphasis is by word choice and backticks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-fork prompts: paired divs, shared chip.
rules_evaluated.evidence: paired divs at L45-L53: <div class="rt-code"> hallucination-bakeoff-3 and <div class="rt-cowork"> hallucination-bakeoff-4 differ only in subagent versus agent; one shared intro at L41; neither fork short of the other; labels left to the renderer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Runtime-mechanical scaffolding asymmetry — MORE in less-fluent fork, not less.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the Cowork fork (hallucination-bakeoff-4) is the same length as the Code fork and carries the same parallel-agent mechanics; no terminal-only plumbing is hidden from Cowork users at this beat (no install, no multi-session open), so no extra scaffolding is owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Citation discipline — extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest hallucination-bakeoff-3 detector 3 and apt101-d2-judge-a-real-summary "quote the sentence from the source that supports it exactly, with its file path, or write \"not found\"": the sentence-level integrity check of (b) is built in, and the conventional-wisdom gap is the planted "two claims that use outside/common knowledge" in bakeoff-1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
rules_evaluated.evidence: every Save names directory and filename: module-5/evidence-roster.md, module-5/briefing.md, module-5/claim-pool.md, module-5/detectors/*.md, module-5/scoreboard.md, judges/groundedness-judge.md, team/<my-name>/judge-run.md. No naked filename; every Save line in the bakeoff-1..5 and judge-run bodies carries a directory.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c -E "/Users|^cd |~/" over bakeoff-1..8 bodies -> 0; paths are session-root relative (module-5/, ./crux.md); no prompt's intent is to change directory.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `subagent` allowed in prompt blocks; explain why after prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: subagent used where isolation matters (bakeoff-1, -3); the why follows the fence in body: L31 "Your main session stays blind, so it cannot quietly help the checks along." and L41 "run in its own subagent and writing to its own file". Cowork runtime says agent (L41, bakeoff-4).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: every Save has a downstream reader: briefing and roster read by claim-pool and detectors; claim-pool by detectors; detectors by the scorer; scoreboard by the judge-writer (bakeoff-8); real-summary.md by apt101-d2-judge-a-real-summary; judge-run.md by keep and run tonight (L121). No (c)-only writes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `
rules_evaluated.evidence: labels are renderer-generated from registry frontmatter dest: Claude Code; the source has no hand-typed **Prompt** (grep -c "^\*\*Prompt\*\*" -> 0), so no custom label can break decoratePrompts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: the ready prompt starts "I'll name a research summary below" and the judge run starts "Run judges/groundedness-judge.md on my real summary": both are normal work requests, not "Ask me which files...". The benchmark prompts are protocol, which is the lesson; the one "If not, ask me for the summary file" is a bounded fallback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: all ten student-copied prompts are registry markers (grep -c "{{prompt:" on the file -> 10 markers, 0 inline **Prompt** blocks); bodies live in curriculum/prompts/<key>.md with matching frontmatter.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: read in isolation, the fences carry their own bindings: bakeoff-1 names crux.md, stances, roster limits and save paths; bakeoff-3/-5 list every input path and the strict substring rule; judge-a-real-summary carries the ask-me fallback. Closest: `<my-name>` unresolved in isolation, covered by the team-folder convention; not a missing disambiguation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest hallucination-bakeoff-5 is the widest prompt but is split by move: reference adjudication, per-detector steps 1-4, scoreboard table, winner rule, recommendation line, each a paragraph; the ready and judge-run prompts are two to four short paragraphs. Condensed-in-a-fence carve-out applies to the detector paragraphs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest L25 lead-in "pick a bounded set of evidence, write an overreaching briefing in a separate worker" against the fence opening "Spawn one subagent to create the benchmark target." shares the subagent-writes-briefing shape without echoing verbs; L98 "run the judge on it against the sources it claims to draw on" rhymes with "Run judges/groundedness-judge.md on my real summary, against its sources."; L74 "the usual way of checking a research summary" rhymes with "the classic way". No pre-paste guard or surprise-pedagogy fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: session boundary read from the body: team lead runs phases 1-4 in the one session opened at the start of the day (L9), so back-references to module-5 files hold; phase 5 is each on their own laptop (L94) and its fence carries paths and the ask-me fallback. "this briefing" in bakeoff-7 is anchored by module-5/briefing.md confirmed in bakeoff-1; no curriculum-coined label (second-pass, send-off) reaches a fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: bakeoff-1 saves then "Only confirm that module-5/evidence-roster.md and module-5/briefing.md exist" (artifact first, confirm last); bakeoff-7 ends "Wait for my one-sentence answer before we move to saving the judge" with no artifact pending. No STOP follows a load-bearing write.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Long-running prompts stream progress — never go silent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: dose first: L43 frames over-run as the anomaly ("If one starts reading far beyond the evidence, stop it, steer it narrower, then say \"continue\"") and hands the student the narrowing move in body beside the fence, which discharges the proactive half; the premature-stop gap belongs to pedagogy 48.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.

suggestions.now: All four run at once. If one starts reading far beyond the evidence, stop it, steer it narrower, then say *"continue"*.
suggestions.proposed: All four run at once. If one starts reading far beyond the evidence, stop it, steer it narrower, then say *"continue"*. If one finishes fast with almost nothing flagged, tell it *"there is more here"* and let it keep going.

suggestions.now: Turn the post-its over. Whoever called it says what they saw that the others didn't; whoever missed says what they trusted instead.
Then ask Claude to get it ready, and say which claim you would bet is unsupported before any judge exists.
suggestions.proposed: Drop the summary after the colon, then the claim you would bet is unsupported before any judge exists.

suggestions.now: Then tell your two teammates which line it was, and whether the judge caught the claim you bet on. "The agent got this wrong" is the sentence.
suggestions.proposed: Then tell your two teammates which line it flagged, or that it came back clean, and whether the judge caught the claim you bet on.

suggestions.now: It found something in a summary nobody planted anything in, and two of you know whether it caught the claim you would have bet on.
suggestions.proposed: On a summary nobody planted anything in, it either found a line to doubt or came back clean, and two of you know whether it caught the claim you would have bet on.

suggestions.now: Phase 5: the real summary comes back clean.
suggestions.proposed: Opening phase: the bet is vague or already checked (recover: ask for the one claim they would quote, with the reason in their words, and tell them not to check it). Phase 5: the real summary comes back clean.
